discovery: Discovery of high-harmonic generation in solids and lightwave-driven control of electrons in crystals

nominees.name: Shambhu Ghimire
nominees.affiliation: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Stanford PULSE Institute, USA

nominees.name: David A. Reis
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

subfield: Ultrafast and strong-field physics of condensed matter (attosecond science)
motivation: Ghimire and Reis (2011) showed that non-perturbative high-order harmonics are generated in bulk crystals, overturning the belief that strong-field harmonic generation belonged only to gases. Huber's subcycle-resolved experiments showed that intense terahertz and mid-infrared fields drive Bloch electrons coherently through the Brillouin zone, with interband polarization and dynamical Bloch oscillations producing the emission. Together these results created a new field. Solid-state harmonics now serve as an all-optical probe of band structure, Berry curvature, topology and correlation, and they are the basis of lightwave electronics operating at petahertz clock rates. The work links attosecond AMO physics to condensed matter and has changed how we understand light-matter interaction in extended systems. It has also posed precise theoretical questions, now tested quantitatively through simulations, about electron trajectories, dephasing and many-body effects. It naturally extends the 2023 attosecond prize into the solid state.
